A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OmniSIFT work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched, including the additional Appendix D.5 in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, efficiency measurements, ablations and qualitative analyses of OmniSIFT, including results in Appendices C and D.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds FASTAV comparisons, Qwen3-Omni transfer experiments, budget-allocation tests and alternative audio-selector evaluations.

M1.justification: The documented VGAS scoring procedure changes: v1 feeds the cross-attention output H into the scoring MLP, whereas v2 adds the original audio representation Z through a residual connection and scores H + Z. STVP, top-k selection and STE training remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether the original experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use the 107K AVoCaDO training pairs and the same five evaluation benchmarks: DailyOmni, VideoMME with audio, WorldSense, OmniVideoBench and video-SALMONN-2. The new experiments reuse DailyOmni and WorldSense without adding datasets or task scenarios.

E2.justification: Appendix D.5 adds FASTAV as an evaluated external comparator on DailyOmni and WorldSense. Tables 11–12 also introduce adaptive-budget, Direct_attention and Concate_av comparison variants. The original OmniZip, DyCoke, random-pruning and existing ablation comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce Qwen3-Omni with LoRA at 35% retention, FASTAV's 50% middle-layer pruning followed by 20% subsequent pruning, and matched 35% budgets for new design comparisons. These extend the settings; the original splits, metrics, preprocessing and Qwen2.5-Omni protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D.5 substantially extends the analysis beyond the retained component, depth and compression-ratio ablations. It tests transfer to another backbone, whether adaptive chunk budgets improve fixed allocation, and whether direct attention scoring or audio-video concatenation can replace the VGAS design.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The additional results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–8 retain their numerical results, but Tables 9–12 add substantive findings. FASTAV scores 59.4/43.3 versus OmniSIFT's 73.2/50.0 on DailyOmni/WorldSense. Qwen3-Omni scores change from 70.8/50.2 with full tokens to 70.5/48.8 with OmniSIFT, alongside lower latency and memory use. New adaptive-budget and selector variants also underperform the default design. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements to the original results.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the residual representation H-tilde = H + Z and revises the formal saliency-score definition accordingly in Equations 8–9. The spatial and temporal saliency equations, STE approximation and Appendix C complexity reasoning remain unchanged; no proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the central claims about modality-asymmetric two-stage compression, small parameter overhead and strong performance with 25% token retention across five benchmarks. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: New Section 6 identifies sensitivity of precise audio-video alignment to pruning, the absence of cross-chunk temporal modeling, and fixed query-agnostic budgets. The introduction qualifies the visual-dependency rationale, while Appendix D.5 adds interpretations supporting backbone transfer and the efficiency of fixed allocation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, explicitly locates compression inputs after the modality projectors, specifies two-second chunks, and identifies LoRA use for Qwen3-Omni. Existing Appendix B preprocessing, compression ratios and evaluation prompts are unchanged. The repository's contents were not externally verified.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 substantially broadens the review to filtering/correlation, variation-aware, hierarchical streaming and curvature-aware compression, together with holistic-context and spatial-temporal preservation considerations. FASTAV enters the audiovisual positioning, and Section 3.3 explicitly connects STVP's motivation to VidCom2 and TimeChat-Online.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized rewrites in the introduction, related work and method explanations, and adds Limitations, Acknowledgements and Appendix D.5. It also corrects OmniSIFT capitalization in Table 2 and replaces the preprint footer with conference information. The overall narrative and section ordering remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9–12, repositions Figure 5 and Table 3, and makes limited table-formatting changes, including Table 4's first-column heading changing from Method to Benchmark. Figures 1–12 are retained without substantive redesign, and the two-column layout remains.

improvement.justification: The added comparator, backbone-transfer and design experiments strengthen empirical support beyond v1, while explicit limitations and implementation disclosures improve transparency. The gains are incremental: core benchmark results remain unchanged, Qwen3-Omni efficiency savings involve accuracy losses, and the new experiments lack uncertainty estimates and detailed LoRA settings. Overall, v2 provides better-supported and better-qualified evidence without resolving these remaining limitations.
